name: Grapefruit
lede: Grapefruit is a bright coral red, named for the fruit's flush; the books read say little about it, so its history is mostly the library's record.

notes.cite: St Clair, The Secret Lives of Colour, ch. 34
ColorHub library (data/library.json): ISCC-NBS 1955 block 102, Maerz & Paul 1930 pl. 19 L 1 (first recorded 1924), xkcd; CIEDE2000
ColorHub archive field notes for Grapefruit (n=5), 23,781 museum paintings as photographed; data/graph/fieldnotes/g.json

sections.title: A fruit's name
sections.body: The name is an everyday fruit word used as a color word. Paterson's dictionary has no color entry for it, and mentions the fruit only to explain that strawberries hold no straw, just as grapefruit holds no grapes [1]. One book does use it as a description: St Clair calls the hose in a Rubens double portrait of himself and his new wife "grapefruit-colored" [2]. That is the modern author's comparison, not a name Rubens or his time used [2].

sections.title: On the charts
sections.body: The library finds the color in three places: the xkcd color survey, the 1955 ISCC-NBS system (block 102), and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, which first records the name in 1924 on plate 19 L 1 [3]. On a screen the nearest everyday name is [[terracotta]], about seven units away, though the swatch is a good deal pinker and brighter than that [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch color is rare in museum paintings: 5 of 23,781 contain it, about 0.02 per cent, rarer than 73 per cent of our named colors [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so the colors are as photographed [4].
